cards.power: Hold up a future so polished the visitor sees their own face in it. Sell the reflection.
cards.lore: A scale model of tomorrow is easily mistaken for a measurement of it.
cards.gradeReason: Chameleon in bubble = you ARE the reflection being sold. Instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: chameleon gazing into iridescent dome, sees own distorted reflection. Mood: seductive, uncanny.

cards.power: Show the destination as already built. No scaffolding, no mud, no maintenance, no Tuesday.
cards.lore: The render is an argument dressed as a photograph of something that does not yet exist.
cards.gradeReason: 'No scaffolding, no Tuesday' — the absence named is the move. Zero-setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: poodle sitting pristine in perfect glass city plaza, no workers, no weather. Mood: uncannily clean, hollow.

cards.power: Make today feel like a waiting room with bad chairs, so the future feels like rescue.
cards.lore: Re-framing the present as merely an obstacle devalues the only time anyone can actually act in.
cards.gradeReason: Dragonfly in waiting room is soft — metaphor reads conceptually before it performs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: dragonfly slumped on plastic chair in grey waiting room, rainbow door in background. Mood: drained, wistful.

cards.power: Offer the dream. Ask only that they stop looking at the floor and sign.
cards.lore: Awe and scrutiny use different states of mind, and awe is faster.
cards.gradeReason: 'Awe is faster' is a single-sentence PhD thesis. Octopus with pen clinches it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: octopus holding glowing pen over contract scroll, eyes wide in wonder. Mood: dazzled, complicit.

cards.power: Promise that one product retires an entire category of human suffering.
cards.lore: Recasting complex social problems as neat technical fixes flatters the tool and ignores the politics.
cards.gradeReason: Walrus checking HUNGER/LONELINESS/DEATH boxes is great; the logic needs one beat to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: walrus at podium checking off enormous checkbox list including DEATH, city skyline behind. Mood: preposterous, ceremonial.

cards.power: Draw a straight line from now to paradise. Hide the cliffs behind the font.
cards.lore: Roadmaps present uncertain futures as scheduled milestones, borrowing the authority of a train timetable.
cards.gradeReason: Caterpillar on dotted path to UTOPIA sun with cliff gap is strong; slightly standard metaphor.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: fuzzy caterpillar on glowing milestone path, massive cliff gap hidden behind soft mist, UTOPIA sun on far side. Mood: optimistic, treacherous.

cards.power: Let salvation slip one quarter, then another. Keep the faith by keeping the date close.
cards.lore: Breakthroughs said to be a few years away sustain belief precisely by never arriving.
cards.gradeReason: Greyhound chasing 'ALMOST THERE' with crossed-out Q3 2023/2024/2025/SOON = instant recognition.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: racing greyhound mid-sprint, scoreboard of crossed-out launch dates trailing behind it. Mood: frantic, tragicomic.

cards.power: Collect belief up front. Deliver the future on a later invoice, or not at all.
cards.lore: Trading on anticipation is a practice old enough to have a name: vaporware.
cards.gradeReason: 'Vaporware' lore payoff is sharp; hamsters queuing at empty storefront needs reading to fully snap.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: long queue of hamsters clutching pre-order slips outside sealed glass storefront, empty inside. Mood: earnest, futile.

cards.power: Aim everything bright and warm. Let the glare do the editing.
cards.lore: The society of the spectacle dictates that the polished image stands in for and outranks the thing itself.
cards.gradeReason: Moth-to-stage-light is classic; Debord reference requires one more beat of context to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: giant moth drawn toward blinding stage spotlight, backstage chaos invisible in silhouette. Mood: hypnotic, obliterating.

cards.power: Show the one path that works flawlessly. Call it the way it works.
cards.lore: A smooth demo predicts almost nothing about a messy real deployment because it only walks the happy path.
cards.gradeReason: Lemur at keyboard is charming; 'happy path' concept needs one breath to activate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: ring-tailed lemur at keyboard performing perfect demo, wires sparking out of frame. Mood: polished surface, chaos underneath.

cards.power: Reward applause faster than questions. Make doubt feel rude.
cards.lore: In a charged crowd, social proof makes visible enthusiasm self-reinforcing until the clapping becomes the evidence.
cards.gradeReason: Seals clapping with lone owl not clapping — solid image but social proof concept needs moment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: rows of seals mid-applause, single owl sitting still and skeptical among them. Mood: tribal, pressure-cooker.

cards.power: Send them home shining. The details can wait for a calmer head that never arrives.
cards.lore: Positive affect at the moment of decision narrows scrutiny—wonder is an excellent place to hide a clause.
cards.gradeReason: 'Wonder is an excellent place to hide a clause' — devastating line, zero setup needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: euphoric fireflies emerging from conference hall into night, contract fine-print floating unread behind them. Mood: luminous, oblivious.

cards.power: Cast one person as the author of tomorrow. Origin story optional, confidence mandatory.
cards.lore: Charismatic authority rests on belief in the individual, meaning it asks for faith and resists audit by design.
cards.gradeReason: Shoebill in stadium with tiny crowd below is strong; 'resists audit by design' carries the weight.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: towering shoebill bird alone on stadium pitch, distant crowd worshipping. Mood: messianic, lonely at the top.

cards.power: Let brilliance excuse the parts that do not add up yet.
cards.lore: The halo effect allows genius in one domain to be quietly spent as credibility in another.
cards.gradeReason: Peacock with halo holding blank spreadsheet — visual argument IS the critique. G1 without hesitation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: peacock with glowing halo displaying blank grid to admiring audience, glitching tech behind. Mood: reverent, vacuous.

cards.power: Make the goal so large that no particular failure can touch it.
cards.lore: A mission framed as advancing humanity immunizes itself from the accountability a narrow promise would face.
cards.gradeReason: 'FOR A BETTER WIG WORLD' gag is funny but unfalsifiability concept reads conceptual before performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: humpback whale trailing enormous banner through utopian skies, banner text absurdly grandiose. Mood: grand, unaccountable.

cards.power: Offer the crowd a role: believe loudly, and you belong.
cards.lore: Shared identity raises the social cost of doubt and turns scrutiny into something close to betrayal.
cards.gradeReason: Rows of badge-wearing penguins is excellent — identity-as-compliance needs one beat to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: endless rows of badge-wearing penguins in conference hall, single empty chair at edge. Mood: conformist, chilling.

cards.power: Make scarcity feel like status. The line is the product.
cards.lore: Artificial scarcity reads as value, and exclusion reads as quality.
cards.gradeReason: 'The line is the product' — three words, complete thesis. Flamingo at mirror delivers it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: flamingo preening before ornate mirror behind velvet rope, long empty queue behind. Mood: self-satisfied, absurd.

cards.power: Hand out a position. Let people defend their place in a queue to nowhere.
cards.lore: Loss aversion makes people defend their position even when the underlying prospect is poor.
cards.gradeReason: 'YOU ARE NO. 24,991' display + walrus clutching ticket = visceral recognition. Table-instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: panicked walrus gripping numbered ticket while board displays its enormous queue number. Mood: resigned, defensive.

cards.power: Turn each believer into a recruiter. Growth disguised as generosity.
cards.lore: Referral mechanics convert enthusiasm into distribution, making the crowd mistake marketing for sharing.
cards.gradeReason: Ants passing glowing orb is charming; 'mistake marketing for sharing' requires the lore read.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: chain of ants passing glowing referral orb across landscape, each ant smiling, unaware. Mood: earnest, algorithmic.

cards.power: Reward the faithful with a slightly nicer waiting room.
cards.lore: Tiered access grants small status upgrades that feel like progress while the destination stays exactly as far away.
cards.gradeReason: Sloth in velvet chair beside chained door is good; 'destination stays exactly as far away' needs the lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: contented sloth in plush armchair next to EARLY ACCESS TIER sign, heavy chained door still locked behind. Mood: pampered, stranded.

cards.power: Keep the payoff one horizon away, always visible, never closer.
cards.lore: A perpetual soon exploits hyperbolic discounting by keeping the prize psychologically near while practically distant.
cards.gradeReason: Giant tortoise on endless rainbow road — 'always visible, never closer' is the move and it's visible.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: ancient tortoise on infinite rainbow path, golden horizon retreating at exactly its pace. Mood: patient, futile.

cards.power: Promise the better you arrives bundled with the better thing.
cards.lore: The future self becomes a product, and the present self is cast as a defect to be upgraded away.
cards.gradeReason: 'Present self as defect to be upgraded away' — hermit crab seeing shell-upgrade reflection nails it cold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: hermit crab in battered can looking in mirror, seeing itself in shining golden shell. Mood: aspirational, melancholy.

cards.power: Trade a real Tuesday for an imagined someday, on repeat.
cards.lore: Every hour spent anticipating is an hour not lived—an opportunity cost that compounds invisibly.
cards.gradeReason: Rat on pile of LATER notebooks reads as visual metaphor before it invites performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: frantic rat buried in tower of LATER notebooks, calendar pages swirling overhead. Mood: compulsive, invisible loss.

cards.power: When someday slips, sell the vow again at full price.
cards.lore: Sustained belief is maintained by re-committing rather than re-evaluating, avoiding the pain of sunk cost.
cards.gradeReason: Bluebird at gilded shrine is evocative; sunk cost mechanism needs lore to complete the move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: bluebird painting gold shrine altar for the third time, fresh votive candles around older half-melted ones. Mood: ritual, avoidant.

cards.power: Frame every question as a failure of imagination.
cards.lore: Reframing criticism as small-mindedness discredits the questioner without engaging the question.
cards.gradeReason: Hippo raising hand among colorful excited animals = the questioner already feels the cold. Instant.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: grey hippo with raised hand among technicolor celebrating animals, all others turning away. Mood: socially costly, precise.

cards.power: Sort skeptics into the past tense. They do not get it yet.
cards.lore: The modern slur misnames a labor argument about power as an ignorant fear of progress.
cards.gradeReason: Mammoth in museum case labelled THE PAST while modern animals use gadgets — image makes the argument.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: woolly mammoth sealed in museum display case while animals with devices point and laugh. Mood: diagnostic, cruel-funny.

cards.power: Make asking feel like leaving the room. Most people stay.
cards.lore: The fear of social exclusion is processed like physical pain, making dissent genuinely costly.
cards.gradeReason: Wolf alone while fox/raccoon/deer warm by fire — strong image but social pain mechanism needs a beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: lone wolf in cold darkness, group of animals gathered at warm fire in distance. Mood: aching isolation, silencing.

cards.power: Welcome the doubter back warmly. Belief tastes sweeter after surrender.
cards.lore: Following the relief of cognitive dissonance, former doubters defend the new belief more strongly than those who never doubted.
cards.gradeReason: Ostrich emerging from hole celebrated by pastel animals — cognitive dissonance mechanism is the engine.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: ostrich pulling head from ground to celebratory confetti shower, eyes shining with newly minted belief. Mood: relieved, fervent.

cards.power: Lower the pulse. Optimism as a sedative, dosed in keynotes.
cards.lore: A hopeful pitch amplifies our natural optimism bias into comfortable, paralyzed inaction.
cards.gradeReason: 'IT WILL BE FINE' neon + capybara soaking = optimism-as-sedative is the image, not the caption.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: blissful capybara soaking in hot spring, glowing 'IT WILL BE FINE' sign reflected in steam. Mood: sedated, warm-trap.

cards.power: Fuse rebel optimism with market faith until questioning either feels like questioning freedom.
cards.lore: Treating technological progress as inherently liberating smoothly conceals who actually wins and loses.
cards.gradeReason: Seal balancing peace symbol + money arrow + wind turbines = the contradiction IS the image. Zero setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: smiling seal juggling peace sign, dollar graph arrow, and wind turbine against utopian skyline. Mood: cheerfully contradictory.

cards.power: Comfort so complete that nobody reaches for the wheel.
cards.lore: Reassurance that progress is automatic reduces the felt need to act; agency becomes optional.
cards.gradeReason: Koala asleep at wheel with DO NOT DISTURB is strong; 'agency becomes optional' needs one breath.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: koala asleep at car steering wheel, DO NOT DISTURB crown on head, car floating in pastel clouds. Mood: passive, drifting.

cards.power: Keep them hopeful, seated, and exactly where you left them.
cards.lore: When optimism is detached from action, it functions solely to maintain the status quo.
cards.gradeReason: Panda eating bamboo with LATER signs is excellent; detached-optimism-as-status-quo needs the lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: panda contentedly eating bamboo in colourful living room, LATER signs blocking every exit. Mood: comfortable, inert.

cards.power: Present the picture of the thing as the thing.
cards.lore: The mind treats vivid representation as proxy evidence of reality.
cards.gradeReason: Lyrebird painting phone on easel in ruined workshop = picture IS the thing. Five-word power, one image.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: lyrebird carefully painting a phone on canvas in rubble-filled studio, finished render gleaming. Mood: meticulous, hollow.

cards.power: Show the same working corner from forty angles. Imply the whole.
cards.lore: Repeated exposure to a single polished fragment makes it feel like a finished system.
cards.gradeReason: Dung beetle rolling glowing sphere in glass dome — 'same corner, forty angles' is the exact visual.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: dung beetle proudly rolling single gleaming sphere in rotating glass dome, observers seeing it from every angle. Mood: thorough, partial.

cards.power: Skip the part where it survived contact with a real week.
cards.lore: The absent record of ordinary operation is always the most important missing document.
cards.gradeReason: Secretary bird at gallery with IN USE tag on empty frame is clever; 'real week' concept needs one beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: secretary bird gesturing at empty gilded frame with IN USE tag, other frames vaguely promising. Mood: evasive, bureaucratic.

cards.power: Let the feeling of progress stand in for the measurement of it.
cards.lore: When momentum is conveyed through tone rather than metrics, the feeling arrives first and satisfies.
cards.gradeReason: Quokka at control panel with smiley sun dial — vibes-as-dashboard is the image. No explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: gleeful quokka at mission control, all dials replaced by mood-emoji readouts, smiley sun as key metric. Mood: frictionless, unaccountable.

cards.power: Promise a life with no edges, no effort, no callus.
cards.lore: The easiest option steadily wins not because it is best, but because it asks the least.
cards.gradeReason: Snail on iridescent bubble is visually pretty but metaphor requires unpacking before it performs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: snail gliding on perfect soap bubble, landscape without friction below, edge of bubble paper-thin. Mood: effortless, fragile.

cards.power: Let the device do the reaching. Keep the hand on the glass.
cards.lore: Skills offloaded to tools erode through disuse—a documented trade of capability for ease.
cards.gradeReason: T-rex with tiny wired prosthetic arm touching tablet = strong visual; skill-atrophy lore needed to snap.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: T-rex with tiny wired prosthetic arm tapping tablet, own arms withered further. Mood: enabling, atrophying.

cards.power: What you never lift, you slowly cannot.
cards.lore: Frictionlessness has a hidden long-term cost paid in lost ability through disuse atrophy.
cards.gradeReason: Goat choosing escalator while stone stairs cobweb — image is crisp; disuse atrophy needs the lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: mountain goat stepping onto escalator beside ancient cobwebbed stone stairs. Mood: comfort choosing itself, quietly eroding.

cards.power: Sell ease so total it quietly removes the option of effort.
cards.lore: When the effortful path is engineered away, a life optimized for comfort loses access to the difficulty that builds skill.
cards.gradeReason: Manatee in rainbow hammock: ease = hammock that ate the exit. Embodiment is immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: enormous manatee sinking luxuriously into rainbow hammock, exits on all sides grown shut with vines. Mood: supremely comfortable, trapped.

cards.power: Frame every problem as a thing the next release will fix.
cards.lore: Defining progress as the next product keeps attention on acquisition and off of repair.
cards.gradeReason: Magpie with NEW box over OLD/OBSOLETE bin is sharp; acquisition-over-repair mechanism needs the lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: magpie triumphantly clutching iridescent NEW box, OLD box full of unsolved problems labelled OBSOLETE below. Mood: perpetually forward, never fixing.

cards.power: Make replacement feel like growth. Discard the old, including the lesson.
cards.lore: Planned obsolescence designs products to be replaced rather than maintained.
cards.gradeReason: Raccoon feeding tools into solar conveyor is fun; 'discard the lesson' is where the card earns its keep.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: raccoon cheerfully tossing tools onto blazing conveyor belt marked RECYCLE, same tools emerging shiny-new on other end. Mood: enthusiastic, amnesiac.

cards.power: Movement without arrival, billed monthly.
cards.lore: Due to hedonic adaptation, each upgrade delivers a brief lift before resetting the wanting.
cards.gradeReason: 'Movement without arrival, billed monthly' — five words, subscription economy demolished. Hamster confirms.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: exhausted hamster sprinting on premium treadmill, BILLED MONTHLY display ticking, scenery never changing. Mood: effortful, pointless.

cards.power: Reward staying on the treadmill with a faster treadmill.
cards.lore: Loyalty systems convert repeat consumption into identity, masking escalation as belonging.
cards.gradeReason: Camel on stacked Diamond/Platinum/Gold stairs = faster treadmill AS the reward. Tautology visible.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: camel climbing tier stairs from Bronze to Diamond, each step a slightly shinier treadmill. Mood: aspirational, circular.

cards.power: Borrow against today to furnish a tomorrow that ships late.
cards.lore: Continually deferring satisfaction spends the present as a means, never an end.
cards.gradeReason: Beaver building house of credit/debt/borrow cards is rich visual; 'ships late' lore grounds the move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: beaver carefully stacking house of credit cards labelled DEBT/FUTURE/BORROW, rainbow outside, structure swaying. Mood: industrious, precarious.

cards.power: Charge attention as rent on a building with no keys.
cards.lore: Attention spent on anticipation is a finite resource drained without return.
cards.gradeReason: Woodpecker at attention meter + locked door is inventive but 'rent on building with no keys' needs unpacking.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: woodpecker pecking at attention gauge while ornate door stays locked, gauge needle dropping. Mood: metered, draining.

cards.power: Add up the Tuesdays spent in the waiting room.
cards.lore: The cost of perpetual anticipation is invisible because it is paid in ordinary, un-itemized hours.
cards.gradeReason: Squirrel writing 'WAITED/WAITED/STILL WAITING' on infinite receipt is poignant; invisibility needs the lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: squirrel writing on endless receipt scroll, each line reading WAITED, Tuesday after Tuesday scrolling off table. Mood: careful, invisible cost.

cards.power: Present the total gently, after the lights are warm and the doubt is gone.
cards.lore: Costs disclosed amid positive affect at the close of a pitch receive the least scrutiny.
cards.gradeReason: Pigeon delivering invoice to warm-lit table is quietly sharp; positive-affect mechanism needs the lore read.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: cooing pigeon sliding $ INFINITE + TAX invoice under warm lamplight to unsuspecting recipient. Mood: warm, gently predatory.

cards.power: Remove every visible seam, so the labor and the trade-offs disappear.
cards.lore: Hiding the seams of a system hides its workings, leaving users unable to contest what they use.
cards.gradeReason: Armadillo curled into perfect sphere rolling blind = hidden seam IS the form. Instant body knowledge.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: armadillo rolled into flawless ball careening across landscape, all seams invisible, joints concealed. Mood: smooth, unknowable.

cards.power: Leave no room for a question. If you cannot ask, you are inside the pitch.
cards.lore: A presentation that absorbs every objection in advance leaves no opening for genuine inquiry.
cards.gradeReason: 'If you cannot ask, you are inside the pitch' — axolotl in bubble = perfect enclosure of the idea.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: bewildered axolotl sealed in pristine bubble, cracks forming from outside questions bouncing off. Mood: airtight, no exit.

cards.power: Offer one path forward and call it the future.
cards.lore: When only one route is presented, a manufactured choice is being disguised as an inevitability.
cards.gradeReason: Capybara on map with single glowing arrow is clean; 'manufactured choice as inevitability' needs lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: capybara studying map with single illuminated route, all alternative paths blacked out. Mood: confident, foreclosed.

cards.power: The shinier it is, the harder you should look for the floor.
cards.lore: Sufficiently advanced presentation acts like magic, and magic works precisely by hiding the mechanism.
cards.gradeReason: Best single line in the deck. Crow with gleaming orb = corvid wisdom about surfaces. No setup needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: crow circling a blinding iridescent sphere, tilting head to find where it stands. Mood: skeptical, drawn, searching.

cards.power: Name every quiet if the promise stands on.
cards.lore: Surfacing the load-bearing ifs a pitch keeps hidden is the core of a pre-mortem audit.
cards.gradeReason: Giraffe with IF/IF/IF tower is conceptually accurate but 'quiet if' phrasing needs unpacking at table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: giraffe peering at tower of IF blocks holding up impossible utopian structure, each block labeled. Mood: analytical, precarious.

cards.power: Find the one assumption that, if false, drops the whole roof.
cards.lore: Identifying the single most fragile assumption tells you more than admiring the finished facade ever could.
cards.gradeReason: Rhino in crumbling arch = one creature, one keystone, entire structure. Embodiment is the card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: rhinoceros standing in cracked triumphal arch, entire facade held by its presence alone. Mood: load-bearing, precarious.

cards.power: Ask who is already paid whether or not tomorrow arrives.
cards.lore: Many who sell a future are compensated on the promise rather than the delivery; for them, arrival is optional.
cards.gradeReason: Vulture receiving REWARDS bag over crowd is sharp; 'arrival is optional' mechanism needs the lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: vulture in spotlight receiving bulging REWARDS bag from podium while crowd below cheers for a future not yet delivered. Mood: compensated regardless.

cards.power: Hold the brochure up to the light. Count the things that have to be true. Notice how many are not.
cards.lore: A promise is only as sound as its hidden assumptions.
cards.gradeReason: FrizzleBob pulling curtain on unfinished city = perfect closer. Power IS the instruction. Exhibition gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor cartoon. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit pulling back billboard curtain to reveal unfinished scaffold city behind glossy render. Mood: revelatory, impish.

verdict: Forget Utopia is the sharpest analytical deck in the corpus — 'awe and scrutiny use different states of mind, and awe is faster' is a university lecture in nine words that plays as a card. The naming convention ('The ___') is perfectly consistent across all 56 cards, and the lore writing reaches a level of economy the rest of the corpus rarely touches. Minor weakness: artwork style shifts slightly between earlier pages (busier, more cluttered) and the cleaner mid-deck pages, and six cards require the lore read before they fully perform. Exhibition-ready: YES.
blurb: A card deck that names the rhetorical moves used to sell futures that never arrive. For anyone who has ever stood in a line to nowhere and wondered exactly how they got there.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — FrizzleBob vandalizing a utopian billboard with a paintbrush while cartoon bugs wreak havoc — meta-commentary as cover image, pitch-perfect
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — FORGET UTOPIA in full caps comic-bold: punchy, memorable, controversy-adjacent in the best way
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Satirical destruction of the glossy sell = exactly what the deck delivers on every page
coverQA.coverOriginality: 5 — Billboard-within-billboard being actively subverted by the deck's own mascot is a genuinely original cover gesture
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — Strong in exhibition context; speech bubble 'Read the small print last. They're counting on that.' is shareable on its own
coverQA.coverNote: Best cover in the exhibition trio. The meta-layer — FrizzleBob painting over the utopian vision that the deck then dissects — is conceptually tight. Speech bubble 'Step inside the future that is already finished' does double work as hook and thesis statement.

notes: 15 pages: 1 cover + 14 story pages x 4 cards = 56 cards, matches exhibition 14-position spine exactly. No RAF mechanics. Decorative margin elements (BLÖDSINN!, KayfaBONGO!, HUMBUG!, Stay fluffy!, LULLABY LIES, WAKE UP?!, NOTHING TO SEE HERE, NO ESCAPE!, FAKE IT TIL YOU BREAK IT!) add tonal flavor without disrupting readability. Final page tagline 'Forget Utopia. Stay fluffy!' is a strong standalone. Artwork shifts from slightly busier style on pages 2-3 to cleaner watercolor on later pages — acceptable variation. Power/lore text is small in PDF render; verify legibility at exhibition print scale.

urgent: Verify power/lore text legibility at exhibition print size — very small in PDF render
quickWins: Use 'Forget Utopia. Stay fluffy!' tagline from page 15 on card backs or exhibition label copy
The Shine Test and The Core Question would make strong pull-quote prints for exhibition wall
niceToHave: Add card numbers for visitor reference and discussion facilitation
Consider whether page 2-3 artwork density matches later pages at final exhibition scale

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: FORGET UTOPIA – Fifty-Six Cards That Scratch the Shine Off the Future They Keep Selling You (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Every bright future arrives pre-lit. Turn off their lamp and look at what is actually standing in the room.

Thirty years ago somebody bottled the promise and called it the California Ideology: hand the market a microchip and everyone walks free, no cost, no losers, paradise on a release schedule. You are still standing inside that pitch. The free tomorrow keeps getting demoed and never quite ships, and the running you do to deserve it never lets you arrive, because arrival was never the product. The pitch was. This is the FORGET wing of the Hannover triptych, the panel that walks off the set where the rescue gets filmed. No savior is cast. No clean utopia is on the way. The shine was the whole show.

This is Social Story Wrestling run as a shine test. You read a card aloud, the table rules on whether the promise under it survives a fingernail or just smears, and the gleaming tomorrow has to stand under a working bulb and account for itself.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Forget Utopia Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring The Shine Test (the scratch you run across any promised paradise to learn if it is paint or structure), The California Ideology (the thirty-year-old sales pitch that quietly swapped liberation for a subscription), and The Treadmill (the future engineered so you run harder to stay exactly where you already are).
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the part where every card can claim anything until the room calls the bluff. Cut on the dotted lines, shuffle, and start the match.
- The Render Walk: fourteen story pages, four cards each, working down from the first glossy horizon to The Signature Line that signs off the sell, and landing on The Core Question you carry off the table and into your week.

This wing hangs on the left of the triptych. Ignore walks past the fear machine in the middle, Embrace picks up the pencil on the right, and Forget clears the ground they both stand on: it takes the rescue fantasy down off the wall so there is room to build something that holds. Read a column straight down and one question gets three answers. The whole triptych lives at protopians.substack.com. Kill the lamp, bring the cards, and make the future show you its receipts.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"A future that only works under good lighting was built to be admired, not lived in."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
